```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(scater)
library(scran)
library(batchelor)
library(BiocSingular)
library(TSCAN)
library(patchwork)
library(DT)

library(scatterpie)
library(ggrepel)
source(paste0(params$project_dir, "/src/scRNA_seq_functions.R"))
```

TSCAN pseudotime for the `r params$lineage` germ cell clusters. The lineage is
`female`, `male`, or `all`, which orders every germ cluster in one tree.
`18_germ_pseudotime_monocle3.Rmd` computes pseudotime for the same cells with
monocle3, and `knit_17_18_pseudotime.sh` knits both documents for each lineage.

Clusters named in `split_by_subcluster` are subclustered within this document
and enter the tree as their subclusters.

Stage and collection date vary together in this dataset, so the ordering is not
shown to be developmental. The library composition of each node and the variance
in pseudotime explained by library are reported with the result.

```{r}
lineage = as.character(params$lineage)
if (!lineage %in% c("female", "male", "all"))
  stop("lineage must be 'female', 'male' or 'all', not '", lineage, "'")

clusters = trimws(strsplit(as.character(switch(lineage,
  female = params$female_clusters,
  male   = params$male_clusters,
  all    = params$all_clusters)), ",")[[1]])
clusters = clusters[nzchar(clusters)]

object_dir      = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", params$results_date,
                         "_no_doublets")
# atlas_suffix picks which atlas to read. "" is 13, "_no_technical_genes" is 13b.
atlas_dir       = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", params$results_date,
                         "_atlas", params$atlas_suffix)
results_dir     = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", params$results_date,
                         "_pseudotime_tscan_", lineage, params$atlas_suffix)
Robject_out_dir = paste0(results_dir, "/Robjects")
if (!dir.exists(Robject_out_dir)) dir.create(Robject_out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

label_file = paste0(atlas_dir, "/cell_cluster_labels.csv")
if (!file.exists(label_file))
  stop("missing ", label_file, ". Run 13_atlas_and_stage_correspondence.Rmd first.")

cell_labels      = read.csv(label_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
all.sce          = readRDS(paste0(object_dir, "/all.sce.Rds"))
gene_description = read.csv(paste0(object_dir, "/gene_descritption.csv"),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Gene, .keep_all = TRUE)

lib_cols = c("Female" = "#FF6DB6", "Male" = "#006ddb",
             "Undifferentiated.1" = "#009292", "Undifferentiated.2" = "#b66ddf")
```

```{r}
# Read here rather than at the point of use, because the checks on the annotated
# run's nodes happen before the corrected space exists.
tech       = technical_gene_ids(gene_description)
mito_ids   = tech$mito
rrna_ids   = tech$rrna
ribo_ids   = tech$ribo
tech_genes = tech$all

# The pipeline computed subsets_Mito_percent before the cells were filtered on
# it, so that is the number the filtering was applied to and the one to report.
# Recomputing it here from the annotation would be a second, unvalidated
# definition of the same quantity.
mito_src = try(dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(all.sce, function(x) {
  cd = as.data.frame(colData(x))
  if (!"subsets_Mito_percent" %in% colnames(cd)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(barcode = colnames(x), pct_mito = cd$subsets_Mito_percent,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})), silent = TRUE)

have_mito_src = !inherits(mito_src, "try-error") && is.data.frame(mito_src) &&
                nrow(mito_src) > 0
```

`r paste0(format(length(mito_ids), big.mark = ","), " mitochondrially encoded genes, ", length(rrna_ids), " cytoplasmic rRNA genes and ", format(length(ribo_ids), big.mark = ","), " ribosomal proteins are identified from the annotation. ", if (have_mito_src) "Percent mitochondrial is taken from subsets_Mito_percent in the per-library objects, which is the quantity the cells were filtered on upstream." else "**subsets_Mito_percent was not found in the per-library objects**, so percent mitochondrial is recomputed here from the annotation and may not match the filter applied upstream.", " Cytoplasmic 28S and 18S rRNA are counted separately, because they are not mitochondrial and are abundant enough to distort that fraction if folded into it.")`

```{r}
# The marker sets are read here rather than at the point of use, because the
# somatic check scores cells that are removed before the corrected space exists.
s1_sets = read.csv(paste0(params$project_dir, "/data/", params$marker_file),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(loc_id = trimws(loc_id), origin = "S1 sheet")

extra_file = as.character(params$extra_marker_file)
extra_path = paste0(params$project_dir, "/data/", extra_file)
have_extra = nzchar(extra_file) && file.exists(extra_path)

all_sets = if (have_extra) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(s1_sets,
                   read.csv(extra_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
                     dplyr::mutate(loc_id = trimws(loc_id), origin = "extra"))
} else s1_sets

set_origin = all_sets %>%
  dplyr::distinct(CellTypeMarkerSet, origin) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CellTypeMarkerSet) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(origin = paste(sort(unique(origin)), collapse = ", "),
                   .groups = "drop")

# A set whose genes all sit inside another set is not a separate measurement.
# Scoring high on it says nothing about it that the larger set does not already
# say. The one-gene sets are where this bites.
set_genes = lapply(split(all_sets$loc_id, all_sets$CellTypeMarkerSet), unique)
set_containment = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(set_genes), function(a)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(names(set_genes), a), function(b)
    if (length(set_genes[[a]]) > 0 && all(set_genes[[a]] %in% set_genes[[b]]))
      data.frame(set = a, contained_in = b, n_genes = length(set_genes[[a]]),
                 genes = paste(sort(set_genes[[a]]), collapse = ", "),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    else NULL))))

# carried onto every set-score table, so a contained set is flagged where it is
# read rather than in a note further up the page
set_flag = if (nrow(set_containment) > 0) {
  set_containment %>%
    dplyr::group_by(set) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(contained_in = paste(sort(contained_in), collapse = ", "),
                     .groups = "drop")
} else data.frame(set = character(0), contained_in = character(0),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# one row per marker gene per group, for the bubble plots. A gene belonging to
# two sets appears once per set, so the rows line up with sets_df positionally.
marker_bubble_df = function(lc, groups, sets_df) {
  present = sets_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(CellTypeMarkerSet, loc_id, symbol) %>%
    dplyr::filter(loc_id %in% rownames(lc))
  groups  = as.character(groups)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(unique(groups), function(gr) {
    m = as.matrix(lc[present$loc_id, groups == gr, drop = FALSE])
    data.frame(group          = gr,
               set            = present$CellTypeMarkerSet,
               gene           = present$loc_id,
               symbol         = present$symbol,
               n_cells        = sum(groups == gr),
               pct_expressing = 100 * rowMeans(m > 0),
               mean_logexpr   = rowMeans(m),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}

marker_bubble_plot = function(df, group_levels, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  df = df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
                  label = ifelse(is.na(symbol) | !nzchar(symbol), gene, symbol))
  ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = label,
                 size = pct_expressing, colour = mean_logexpr)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.4, 5)) +
    facet_grid(set ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(strip.text.y     = element_text(angle = 0, size = 6),
          axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 6),
          axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = .2)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
         size = "% expressing", colour = "mean log expression")
}
```

# Cells

```{r}
absent = setdiff(clusters, cell_labels$final_label)
if (length(absent) > 0)
  stop("cluster(s) ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "), " are not in ", label_file,
       ". Labels present: ",
       paste(sort(unique(cell_labels$final_label)), collapse = ", "),
       ". Set the ", lineage, "_clusters parameter from the current labelling.")

lineage_key = cell_labels %>% dplyr::filter(final_label %in% clusters)

# Cells the collaborators annotated as somatic are removed here, before the
# corrected space is built, so they influence neither the embedding nor the
# subclustering. They are identified by barcode from the run that was
# annotated, so this does not depend on the new subclustering agreeing with the
# old numbering. Every lineage holding those cells loses them, including the
# ones whose own subclusters are never annotated.
parse_pairs = function(x) {
  x = trimws(x)
  if (!nzchar(x)) return(character(0))
  kv = strsplit(trimws(strsplit(x, ";")[[1]]), "=")
  setNames(vapply(kv, function(z) trimws(z[2]), character(1)),
           vapply(kv, function(z) trimws(z[1]), character(1)))
}

anno_map  = parse_pairs(params$node_annotation)
drop_anno = trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$drop_annotations), ";")[[1]])
drop_anno = drop_anno[nzchar(drop_anno)]
prev_file = as.character(params$prev_nodes_file)
have_prev = nzchar(prev_file) && file.exists(prev_file)

# The somatic check exists to put expression behind a removal. With
# drop_annotations empty nothing is removed, and its tables would repeat Node
# identity on the same cells, so the whole section is skipped.
do_somatic = have_prev && length(drop_anno) > 0

drop_cells    = character(0)
drop_cell_tab = NULL
# kept so the somatic check can score the removed cells alongside the ones
# that stay
predrop_barcodes = lineage_key$barcode

# read whenever it is available, because the subclustering below uses it to set
# the number of subclusters to look for, which does not depend on any drop
prev_nodes = NULL
if (have_prev) {
  prev_nodes = read.csv(prev_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("barcode", "node") %in% colnames(prev_nodes)))
  prev_nodes$node = as.character(prev_nodes$node)
}

if (!is.null(prev_nodes) && length(drop_anno) > 0) {
  old_drop_nodes = names(anno_map)[anno_map %in% drop_anno]
  absent = setdiff(old_drop_nodes, unique(prev_nodes$node))
  if (length(absent) > 0)
    stop("nodes named by drop_annotations are not in ", prev_file, ": ",
         paste(absent, collapse = ", "), ". Nodes there: ",
         paste(sort(unique(prev_nodes$node)), collapse = ", "))

  drop_cells = prev_nodes$barcode[prev_nodes$node %in% old_drop_nodes]

  drop_cell_tab = prev_nodes %>%
    dplyr::filter(node %in% old_drop_nodes) %>%
    dplyr::count(node, name = "cells_annotated") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(annotation = unname(anno_map[node]),
                  cells_here = vapply(node, function(nd)
                    sum(lineage_key$barcode %in%
                          prev_nodes$barcode[prev_nodes$node == nd]),
                    integer(1)))

  lineage_key = lineage_key %>% dplyr::filter(!(barcode %in% drop_cells))
}

comp_tab = lineage_key %>%
  dplyr::count(final_label, cell_type, library, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = library, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(names(lib_cols))))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(match(final_label, clusters))

write.csv(comp_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_composition.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(comp_tab, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

`r paste0(format(nrow(lineage_key), big.mark = ","), " cells from cluster(s) ", paste(clusters, collapse = ", "), ".")`

```{r, results="asis"}
if (do_somatic) cat(
"## Somatic check

The cells named by `drop_annotations` are removed above on the strength of the
label they were given. This section scores them before they go. The removal then
has expression behind it.

Every node of the annotated run is scored against all the marker sets, somatic
ones included. Grouping is by the node assignment in `prev_nodes_file`. The
values are the depth-normalized ones in the per-library objects. Neither the new
embedding nor the new subcluster numbering enters this. The table therefore
stands whatever the subclustering returns.

The nodes being removed are placed first on the axis. A node that carries a
somatic set and none of the germ sets is the pattern that supports dropping it.
")
```

```{r}
somatic_scores = NULL
somatic_bubble = NULL
somatic_levels = character(0)

if (do_somatic) {
  chk_list = lapply(all.sce, function(x) {
    keep = intersect(colnames(x), predrop_barcodes)
    if (length(keep) == 0) NULL else x[, keep]
  })
  chk_list = chk_list[!vapply(chk_list, is.null, logical(1))]
  # only the marker genes are scored here, so the rest are never materialized
  chk_univ = intersect(Reduce(intersect, lapply(chk_list, rownames)),
                       unique(all_sets$loc_id))
  if (length(chk_univ) == 0)
    stop("none of the marker genes in ", params$marker_file,
         " are present in every library of this lineage.")

  chk_lc = do.call(cbind, lapply(chk_list, function(x)
    logcounts(x)[chk_univ, , drop = FALSE]))

  chk_node = prev_nodes$node[match(colnames(chk_lc), prev_nodes$barcode)]
  keep_chk = !is.na(chk_node)
  chk_lc   = chk_lc[, keep_chk, drop = FALSE]
  chk_node = chk_node[keep_chk]

  # the removed nodes first, then the rest, subclusters before whole clusters
  chk_drop = intersect(names(anno_map)[anno_map %in% drop_anno], chk_node)
  chk_rest = setdiff(unique(chk_node), chk_drop)
  chk_rest = c(sort(chk_rest[grepl("\\.", chk_rest)]),
               sort(chk_rest[!grepl("\\.", chk_rest)]))
  somatic_levels = c(chk_drop, chk_rest)

  chk_sce = SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(logcounts = chk_lc))

  somatic_scores = score_marker_sets(
      chk_sce, chk_node,
      all_sets %>% dplyr::transmute(set = CellTypeMarkerSet, gene = loc_id) %>%
        dplyr::distinct()) %>%
    dplyr::rename(node = group) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(set_origin, by = c("set" = "CellTypeMarkerSet")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(set_flag, by = "set") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(node    = factor(node, levels = somatic_levels),
                  removed = node %in% chk_drop,
                  annotation = unname(anno_map[as.character(node)]),
                  contained_in = tidyr::replace_na(contained_in, ""),
                  mean_logexpr = signif(mean_logexpr, 3),
                  pct_detected = round(pct_detected, 1)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(node, dplyr::desc(mean_logexpr)) %>%
    dplyr::select(node, annotation, removed, set, origin, contained_in,
                  n_genes, n_cells, mean_logexpr, pct_detected)

  write.csv(somatic_scores,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/somatic_check_set_scores.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  # Depth and technical content on the same nodes. Summed per library so the
  # full counts matrix is never assembled, unlike the marker scoring above,
  # which needs only the marker rows.
  old_qc = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(chk_list, function(x) {
    ct = counts(x)
    data.frame(barcode  = colnames(x),
               total    = Matrix::colSums(ct),
               detected = Matrix::colSums(ct > 0),
               mito_g   = Matrix::colSums(ct[intersect(mito_ids, rownames(ct)), ,
                                             drop = FALSE]),
               rrna     = Matrix::colSums(ct[intersect(rrna_ids, rownames(ct)), ,
                                             drop = FALSE]),
               ribo     = Matrix::colSums(ct[intersect(ribo_ids, rownames(ct)), ,
                                             drop = FALSE]),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct_rrna = 100 * rrna / total,
                  pct_ribo = 100 * ribo / total,
                  node     = prev_nodes$node[match(barcode, prev_nodes$barcode)]) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(node)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(node = factor(node, levels = somatic_levels))

  old_qc = if (have_mito_src) {
    old_qc %>% dplyr::left_join(mito_src, by = "barcode")
  } else old_qc %>% dplyr::mutate(pct_mito = 100 * mito_g / total)

  old_qc_tab = old_qc %>%
    dplyr::group_by(node) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(annotation      = unname(anno_map[as.character(node[1])]),
                     removed         = as.character(node[1]) %in% chk_drop,
                     n_cells         = dplyr::n(),
                     median_total    = round(median(total)),
                     median_detected = round(median(detected)),
                     median_pct_mito = round(median(pct_mito), 1),
                     median_pct_rrna = round(median(pct_rrna), 1),
                     median_pct_ribo = round(median(pct_ribo), 1),
                     .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(node)

  write.csv(old_qc_tab,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/annotated_run_depth_and_technical.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  somatic_bubble = marker_bubble_df(chk_lc, chk_node, all_sets)
  write.csv(somatic_bubble,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/somatic_check_gene_expression.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  datatable(somatic_scores, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
            options = list(pageLength = 20))
}
```

If a node is being removed as a cell type that file was meant to cover, this check cannot speak to it.") else if (have_extra) paste0("Scored against ", dplyr::n_distinct(all_sets$CellTypeMarkerSet), " sets, of which ", paste(sort(setdiff(unique(all_sets$CellTypeMarkerSet), unique(s1_sets$CellTypeMarkerSet))), collapse = ", "), " come from ", extra_file, ".") else ""`

if (!is.null(somatic_bubble)) {
  p_somatic = marker_bubble_plot(
    somatic_bubble, somatic_levels,
    title    = "Marker expression by node of the annotated run",
    subtitle = paste0("removed: ",
                      paste(paste0(chk_drop, " (", anno_map[chk_drop], ")"),

# Nodes

TSCAN builds a minimum spanning tree over node centroids, so it needs at least
two nodes.

```{r}
split_clusters = trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$split_by_subcluster), ",")[[1]])

have_split     = length(split_clusters) > 0

# "prev" takes the subclusters from the run whose subclusters were annotated,
# rather than deriving new ones. With nothing dropped, that run's assignment
# covers exactly the cells in these clusters, so there is nothing to recompute

  stop("subcluster_source is 'prev' but prev_nodes_file is not set or not found: '",
       prev_src, "'. Point it at the pseudotime_per_cell.csv of the annotated run, ",
       "or set subcluster_source to 'recluster'.")

have_sweep = have_split && !reuse_sub

`r if (!have_split) paste0("The ", length(clusters), " selected clusters are the nodes.") else if (reuse_sub) paste0("Cluster(s) ", paste(split_clusters, collapse = ", "), " enter the tree as the subclusters of ", basename(prev_src), ", and every other cluster is one node. No cell is dropped from these clusters, so that assignment covers all of them and there is nothing to recompute. Deriving new subclusters here would produce a different partition, because this lineage's corrected space no longer holds the same cells, and the collaborators' labels would then have to be matched onto it. Taking the groups they were assigned to avoids that entirely. The subclusters are a partition of the earlier space carried forward; the centroids, the tree and the ordering are all computed in the current one.") else paste0("Cluster(s) ", paste(split_clusters, collapse = ", "), " are subclustered in this lineage's corrected space, using only that cluster's cells, and every other cluster is one node. k is the most reproducible value in a subsampling stability sweep that gives at least two subclusters. Setting sub_n_clusters restricts the search to the k values returning that many subclusters, and the most reproducible of those is taken. The sub_k parameter overrides the sweep. The space depends on the lineage, so cluster 5 subclusters from the female and all runs are computed separately and need not match.")`

```{r, eval=reuse_sub}
prev_sub = read.csv(prev_src, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("barcode", "node") %in% colnames(prev_sub)))
prev_sub$node = as.character(prev_sub$node)

sub_assign = list()
chosen_ks  = integer(0)

for (cl in split_clusters) {
  cl_cells = colnames(merged)[merged$final_label == cl]
  old      = prev_sub$node[match(cl_cells, prev_sub$barcode)]

  miss = is.na(old)
  if (any(miss))
    stop("cluster ", cl, ": ", sum(miss), " of ", length(cl_cells),
         " cells have no node in ", prev_src,
         ". Every cell must be assigned there for its subclusters to be reused.")

  pref = paste0("^", cl, "\\.")
  bad  = !grepl(pref, old)
  if (any(bad))
    stop("cluster ", cl, ": ", sum(bad), " of its cells sit in nodes of ",
         prev_src, " that are not its subclusters: ",
         paste(sort(unique(old[bad])), collapse = ", "),
         ". That file describes a different clustering of these cells.")

  sub_assign[[cl]] = setNames(sub(pref, "", old), cl_cells)
  chosen_ks[cl]    = NA_integer_
}

reuse_tab = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(split_clusters, function(cl)
  data.frame(cluster = cl, subcluster = paste0(cl, ".", sub_assign[[cl]]),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE))) %>%
  dplyr::count(cluster, subcluster, name = "n_cells")

datatable(reuse_tab, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15))

```{r, eval=have_sweep}
k_range = as.integer(trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$sub_k_range), ",")[[1]]))
stopifnot(length(k_range) > 0, !anyNA(k_range))

sub_assign  = list()
stab_tabs   = list()
search_tabs = list()
chosen_ks   = integer(0)

for (cl in split_clusters) {
  cl_cells = colnames(merged)[merged$final_label == cl]

  stab_file     = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/subcluster_stability_", cl, ".Rds")
  stab_sig_file = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/subcluster_stability_", cl, "_signature.txt")
  stab_sig      = paste(obj_sig, cl, length(cl_cells), paste(k_range, collapse = ","),
                        params$sub_n_iterations, sep = "|")

  if (file.exists(stab_file) && file.exists(stab_sig_file) &&
      identical(readLines(stab_sig_file, warn = FALSE)[1], stab_sig)) {
    stab = readRDS(stab_file)
  } else {
    # coordinates only, since find_stable_k subsets the object once per iteration
    # column names first: reducedDim<- checks its rownames against them
    lean = SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(), colData = colData(merged)[cl_cells, ])
    colnames(lean) = cl_cells
    reducedDim(lean, "corrected") = reducedDim(merged, "corrected")[cl_cells, , drop = FALSE]

    stab = find_stable_k(lean, k_range = k_range,
                         n_iterations = params$sub_n_iterations,
                         use.dimred = "corrected")
    saveRDS(stab, file = stab_file)
    writeLines(stab_sig, stab_sig_file)
  }

  tab = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(stab, function(z)
    data.frame(cluster = cl, k = z$k, mean_n_clusters = z$mean_n_clusters,
               mean_ari = z$mean_ari, min_ari = z$min_ari)))

  eligible = tab %>% dplyr::filter(mean_n_clusters >= 2, !is.na(mean_ari))

  # k is the most stable value in the sweep. sub_n_clusters restricts the search
  # to the k values returning a given number of subclusters, which is off by
  # default. mean_n_clusters is a mean over subsamples and does not say what the
  # full-data clustering returns, so every candidate k is fitted and counted.
  target = if (as.integer(params$sub_n_clusters) > 0)
    as.integer(params$sub_n_clusters) else NA_integer_

  fit_k = function(k) {
    set.seed(1)
    snn = buildSNNGraph(merged[, cl_cells], k = k, use.dimred = "corrected")
    setNames(igraph::cluster_louvain(snn)$membership, cl_cells)
  }

  if (as.integer(params$sub_k) > 0) {
    k_cl   = as.integer(params$sub_k)
    fits   = setNames(list(fit_k(k_cl)), as.character(k_cl))
    search = data.frame(cluster = cl, k = k_cl, mean_ari = NA_real_,
                        n_clusters = dplyr::n_distinct(fits[[1]]),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    if (nrow(eligible) == 0)
      stop("cluster ", cl, ": no k in the sweep gave two or more subclusters. ",
           "Set sub_k to force a value.")

    cand   = eligible %>% dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_ari))
    fits   = lapply(cand$k, fit_k)
    names(fits) = as.character(cand$k)
    search = data.frame(cluster    = cl,
                        k          = cand$k,
                        mean_ari   = cand$mean_ari,
                        n_clusters = vapply(fits, dplyr::n_distinct, integer(1)),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

    if (is.na(target)) {
      k_cl = search$k[which.max(search$mean_ari)]
    } else {
      ok = search %>% dplyr::filter(n_clusters == target)
      if (nrow(ok) == 0)
        stop("cluster ", cl, ": no k in sub_k_range returns ", target,
             " subclusters. The sweep gives ",
             paste0("k=", search$k, " -> ", search$n_clusters,
                    collapse = "; "),
             ". Widen sub_k_range, set sub_n_clusters to a count the sweep ",
             "reaches, or set sub_k to force a value.")
      k_cl = ok$k[which.max(ok$mean_ari)]
    }
  }

  search$target = target
  search$chosen = search$k == k_cl
  search_tabs[[cl]] = search

  sub_assign[[cl]] = fits[[as.character(k_cl)]]

  stab_tabs[[cl]] = tab
  chosen_ks[cl]   = k_cl
}

stab_tab = dplyr::bind_rows(stab_tabs)
write.csv(stab_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_stability.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(stab_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

```{r, results="asis"}
# Nothing is printed where the subclusters are reused. The note below names the
# file they came from, which is the whole of it.
if (!reuse_sub) cat(
"The collaborators annotated the nodes of an earlier run of this document. The
subclusters of cluster 5 are recomputed here, in a space that no longer contains
12_transformer, so their numbers need not match the ones that were annotated.
Nodes that are whole clusters keep their names and carry their annotation
directly.

Old and new subclusters are matched by the cells they hold. Both runs subcluster
the same cluster 5 cells, so the match is a contingency table rather than a
similarity measure. Each new subcluster takes the annotation of the old
subcluster it shares the most cells with, and the Jaccard for that pair is
reported. A pair below `min_map_jaccard`, a split or a merge stops the
annotation rather than assigning a label the overlap does not support.
")
```

```{r}
parse_pairs = function(x) {
  x = trimws(x)
  if (!nzchar(x)) return(character(0))
  kv = strsplit(trimws(strsplit(x, ";")[[1]]), "=")
  setNames(vapply(kv, function(z) trimws(z[2]), character(1)),
           vapply(kv, function(z) trimws(z[1]), character(1)))
}

# The annotation applies only to the lineages named in annotate_lineages. The
# female run subclusters cluster 5 in its own space, so its numbering is its own
# and the labels from another run do not carry over to it.
anno_lineages = trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$annotate_lineages), ",")[[1]])
do_anno       = lineage %in% anno_lineages

anno_map      = if (do_anno) parse_pairs(params$node_annotation) else character(0)
drop_anno     = if (do_anno)
  trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$drop_annotations), ";")[[1]]) else character(0)
drop_anno     = drop_anno[nzchar(drop_anno)]
prev_file     = as.character(params$prev_nodes_file)
have_prev     = do_anno && nzchar(prev_file) && file.exists(prev_file)
sub_nodes_now = node_levels[grepl("\\.", node_levels)]
```

`r if (!do_anno) paste0("**No annotation is applied to the ", lineage, " lineage.** annotate_lineages is ", params$annotate_lineages, ".") else if (length(anno_map) == 0) "**No annotation is applied.** The node_annotation parameter is empty." else if (length(sub_nodes_now) > 0 && !have_prev) paste0("**Subclusters cannot be annotated.** ", if (nzchar(prev_file)) paste0(prev_file, " was not found.") else "prev_nodes_file is not set.", " Set it to the pseudotime_per_cell.csv of the run the annotation came from. Whole-cluster nodes are still annotated by name.") else ""`

```{r}
map_tab = NULL

# Under subcluster_source = "prev" the nodes already carry her numbering, so
# every label attaches by name and there is nothing to match by overlap.
if (!reuse_sub && have_prev && length(sub_nodes_now) > 0) {
  prev = read.csv(prev_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("barcode", "node") %in% colnames(prev)))

  old_node = setNames(as.character(prev$node), prev$barcode)
  now      = data.frame(barcode = colnames(merged),
                        new = as.character(node_chr),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  now$old  = unname(old_node[now$barcode])

  # only the subclustered cells can move between numbering schemes
  pair = now %>%
    dplyr::filter(new %in% sub_nodes_now, !is.na(old)) %>%
    dplyr::count(new, old, name = "shared")

  if (nrow(pair) == 0)
    stop("no cells matched between the current nodes and ", prev_file,
         ". Check that it is the pseudotime_per_cell.csv of the same lineage.")

  n_new = now %>% dplyr::filter(new %in% sub_nodes_now) %>%
    dplyr::count(new, name = "n_new")
  n_old = now %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(old)) %>%
    dplyr::count(old, name = "n_old")

  # every old-new pair, kept so the check below can say where the cells of an
  # unmatched old subcluster went
  pair_j = pair %>%
    dplyr::left_join(n_new, by = "new") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(n_old, by = "old") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(jaccard = shared / (n_new + n_old - shared))

  map_tab = pair_j %>%
    dplyr::group_by(new) %>%
    dplyr::slice_max(jaccard, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(annotation = unname(anno_map[old]))

  # written before the check below so a run that stops there still leaves the
  # whole contingency table to read
  write.csv(pair_j, file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_annotation_map.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  # the full grid, including pairs that share no cells, so the heatmap below has
  # a value everywhere rather than gaps
  node_ord = function(x) x[order(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("^.*\\.", "", x))),
                                 sub("\\..*$", "", x))]
  overlap_grid = tidyr::expand_grid(new = sub_nodes_now,
                                    old = sort(unique(pair_j$old))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pair_j %>% dplyr::select(new, old, shared),
                     by = c("new", "old")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(shared = tidyr::replace_na(shared, 0L)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(n_new, by = "new") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(n_old, by = "old") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(`percent of the new subcluster` = 100 * shared / n_new,
                  `percent of the old subcluster` = 100 * shared / n_old,
                  `percent of the union (Jaccard)` =
                    100 * shared / (n_new + n_old - shared))

  write.csv(overlap_grid,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_overlap_grid.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  datatable(map_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))),
            rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
}
```

cell of a small old one, and a small slice of a large one, scores low against
both. The three panels below separate that. Read down a column to see what a new
subcluster is made of, and across a row to see where an old one went.
")

The grid is written to subcluster_overlap_grid.csv.")`

```{r}
merge_tab = NULL
split_tab = NULL

if (!is.null(map_tab)) {
  weak  = map_tab$new[map_tab$jaccard < params$min_map_jaccard]
  # one old subcluster winning two new ones is a split
  split = unique(map_tab$old[duplicated(map_tab$old)])
  unlab = map_tab$new[is.na(map_tab$annotation)]
  # an old subcluster that is present in the data but wins nothing is a merge,
  # and its annotation would be lost without a word. Only cluster 5 is
  # subclustered, so only old nodes with a subcluster number are at risk; whole
  # clusters carry their annotation by name and never enter the mapping.
  old_sub     = unique(pair_j$old[grepl("\\.", pair_j$old)])
  droppable   = names(anno_map)[anno_map %in% drop_anno]
  merged_away = setdiff(intersect(old_sub, names(anno_map)),
                        c(map_tab$old, droppable))

  # where the cells of an unmatched old subcluster ended up
  fate = function(olds) paste0(
    pair_j %>%
      dplyr::filter(old %in% olds) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(old, dplyr::desc(shared)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(line = sprintf("      %s -> %s: %d of %d cells, jaccard %s",
                                   old, new, shared, n_old, signif(jaccard, 2))) %>%
      dplyr::pull(line),
    collapse = "\n")

  # A merge is not a failure of the mapping. The clustering simply did not
  # separate two groups the earlier run did, and both labels belong on the node
  # that took the cells. Under on_merge = "combine" the annotations are joined
  # and reported; under "stop" the run halts instead.
  if (length(merged_away) > 0 && identical(as.character(params$on_merge), "combine")) {
    merge_tab = pair_j %>%
      dplyr::filter(old %in% merged_away) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(old) %>%
      dplyr::slice_max(shared, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(annotation = unname(anno_map[old]),
                    kept_share = shared / n_old) %>%
      dplyr::select(old, annotation, absorbed_by = new, shared, n_old,
                    kept_share, jaccard)
    merged_away = character(0)
  }

  # A split is the mirror of a merge and is not a failure either. The clustering
  # resolved finer than the earlier run did inside one annotated group, so both
  # new subclusters are part of that group and both take its label. They stay
  # apart as nodes, because their numbers differ. Under on_split = "stop" the
  # run halts instead.
  if (length(split) > 0 && identical(as.character(params$on_split), "label_both")) {
    split_tab = map_tab %>%
      dplyr::filter(old %in% split) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(old, dplyr::desc(shared)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(share_of_old = shared / n_old) %>%
      dplyr::select(old, annotation, new, shared, n_new, n_old, share_of_old,
                    jaccard)
    split = character(0)
  }

  if (length(weak) > 0 || length(split) > 0 || length(unlab) > 0 ||
      length(merged_away) > 0)
    stop("the annotation cannot be carried over.\n",
         if (length(weak) > 0)
           paste0("  below min_map_jaccard (", params$min_map_jaccard, "): ",
                  paste(weak, collapse = ", "), "\n") else "",
         if (length(split) > 0)
           paste0("  one old subcluster is the best match for more than one new ",
                  "one: ", paste(split, collapse = ", "), "\n",
                  "    the new subclusters holding its cells:\n", fate(split), "\n",
                  "    set on_split to 'label_both' to give them all its label.\n")
         else "",
         if (length(merged_away) > 0)
           paste0("  these old subclusters are the best match for nothing, so ",
                  "their annotation would be lost: ",
                  paste(merged_away, collapse = ", "), "\n",
                  "    their cells are now in:\n", fate(merged_away), "\n",
                  "    set on_merge to 'combine' to join the labels instead.\n")
         else "",
         if (length(unlab) > 0)
           paste0("  no annotation given for the matched old subcluster of: ",
                  paste(unlab, collapse = ", "), "\n") else "",
         "Read the table above and set node_annotation, or raise ",
         "min_map_jaccard deliberately.")
}

# annotation for every node: subclusters through the mapping, whole clusters by
# name, anything left over as itself
node_anno = setNames(node_levels, node_levels)
direct    = intersect(node_levels, names(anno_map))
node_anno[direct] = anno_map[direct]
if (!is.null(map_tab))
  node_anno[map_tab$new] = map_tab$annotation

# a node that absorbed another annotated subcluster carries both labels. The
# components are kept in node_parts so the root can still be named by any one
# of them.
node_parts = as.list(node_anno)
names(node_parts) = node_levels
if (!is.null(merge_tab)) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(merge_tab))) {
    nd = merge_tab$absorbed_by[i]
    node_parts[[nd]] = union(node_parts[[nd]], merge_tab$annotation[i])
  }
  node_anno[names(node_parts)] = vapply(node_parts,
                                        function(z) paste(z, collapse = " / "),
                                        character(1))
}

node_label = ifelse(node_anno == node_levels, node_levels,
                    paste0(node_levels, " ", node_anno))
names(node_label) = node_levels
```

## Depth and technical content

Subclusters that differ by sequencing depth rather than by cell state show a
characteristic pattern. The shallower group's markers are the abundant genes of
the deeper one at lower magnitude, and housekeeping genes climb its marker list.
This section measures depth directly so that reading does not rest on the marker
lists alone.

```{r}
cnt = counts(combined)

qc = data.frame(
  barcode   = colnames(combined),
  node      = as.character(merged$node),
  total     = Matrix::colSums(cnt),
  detected  = Matrix::colSums(cnt > 0),
  pct_rrna  = 100 * Matrix::colSums(cnt[intersect(rrna_ids, rownames(cnt)), , drop = FALSE]) /
                Matrix::colSums(cnt),
  pct_ribo  = 100 * Matrix::colSums(cnt[intersect(ribo_ids, rownames(cnt)), , drop = FALSE]) /
                Matrix::colSums(cnt),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

qc = if (have_mito_src) {
  qc %>% dplyr::left_join(mito_src, by = "barcode")
} else qc %>% dplyr::mutate(
  pct_mito = 100 * Matrix::colSums(cnt[intersect(mito_ids, rownames(cnt)), , drop = FALSE]) /
               Matrix::colSums(cnt))

qc_tab = qc %>%
  dplyr::group_by(node) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_cells = dplyr::n(),
                   median_total    = round(median(total)),
                   median_detected = round(median(detected)),
                   median_pct_mito = round(median(pct_mito), 1),
                   median_pct_rrna = round(median(pct_rrna), 1),
                   median_pct_ribo = round(median(pct_ribo), 1),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(node = factor(node, levels = node_levels)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(node)

write.csv(qc_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/node_depth_and_technical.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(qc_tab, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

```{r}
# Does node membership track depth within a subclustered cluster? Kruskal-Wallis
# on the subclusters alone, plus how far apart the extreme nodes sit.
depth_tests = NULL
if (have_split) {
  depth_tests = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(split_clusters, function(cl) {
    sub = qc %>% dplyr::filter(grepl(paste0("^", cl, "\\."), node))
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(sub$node) < 2) return(NULL)
    med = sub %>% dplyr::group_by(node) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(m = median(total), .groups = "drop")
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("total", "detected", "pct_mito", "pct_rrna", "pct_ribo"), function(v) {
      kt = kruskal.test(sub[[v]] ~ factor(sub$node))
      data.frame(cluster = cl, measure = v,
                 kruskal_p = signif(kt$p.value, 3),
                 fold_range = signif(max(med$m) / min(med$m), 3),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
  if (!is.null(depth_tests)) {
    depth_tests$fold_range[depth_tests$measure != "total"] = NA
    write.csv(depth_tests,
              file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_depth_tests.csv"),
              row.names = FALSE)
    datatable(depth_tests, rownames = FALSE,
              options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
  }
}
```

`r if (is.null(depth_tests)) "" else { tt = depth_tests %>% dplyr::filter(measure == "total"); paste0("Median total counts across the subclusters of cluster ", paste(tt$cluster, collapse = ", "), " differ by a factor of ", paste(tt$fold_range, collapse = ", "), " between the deepest and shallowest node (Kruskal-Wallis p ", paste(tt$kruskal_p, collapse = ", "), "). A large factor here is the signature of a depth split. It does not by itself prove one, because a real cell state can also carry more RNA.") }`

```{r, results="asis"}
if (have_sweep && isTRUE(params$downsample_check)) cat(
"The test that separates the two is below. Counts are downsampled to a common
depth, the subclustering is repeated on the downsampled values, and the result is
compared with the original. A split that survives downsampling is not a depth
split. A split that dissolves is.
")
```

```{r, eval=(have_sweep && isTRUE(params$downsample_check))}
ds_res = NULL

for (cl in split_clusters) {
  cl_cells = colnames(merged)[merged$final_label == cl]
  orig     = as.character(merged$node)[match(cl_cells, colnames(merged))]
  if (dplyr::n_distinct(orig) < 2) next

  sub_cnt = cnt[, cl_cells, drop = FALSE]
  keep_g  = Matrix::rowSums(sub_cnt) > 0

  set.seed(1)
  ds = scuttle::downsampleMatrix(sub_cnt[keep_g, , drop = FALSE],
                                 prop = min(Matrix::colSums(sub_cnt)) /
                                        Matrix::colSums(sub_cnt))
  ds_sce = SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = ds))
  ds_sce = scuttle::logNormCounts(ds_sce)

  dec_ds = scran::modelGeneVar(ds_sce)
  hvg_ds = scran::getTopHVGs(dec_ds, n = 2000)
  set.seed(1)
  ds_sce = scater::runPCA(ds_sce, subset_row = hvg_ds, ncomponents = 30,
                          BSPARAM = BiocSingular::RandomParam())
  set.seed(1)
  snn_ds = buildSNNGraph(ds_sce, k = chosen_ks[cl], use.dimred = "PCA")
  new_ds = igraph::cluster_louvain(snn_ds)$membership

  ds_res[[cl]] = list(
    tab = table(original = orig, downsampled = new_ds),
    row = data.frame(cluster = cl,
                     k = chosen_ks[cl],
                     n_original = dplyr::n_distinct(orig),
                     n_downsampled = dplyr::n_distinct(new_ds),
                     ari = signif(mclust::adjustedRandIndex(orig, new_ds), 3),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

if (!is.null(ds_res)) {
  ds_tab = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ds_res, `[[`, "row"))
  write.csv(ds_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_downsample_check.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  datatable(ds_tab, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
}
```

```{r, eval=(have_sweep && isTRUE(params$downsample_check))}

  cat("\ncluster", cl, "- original subclusters against the downsampled ones\n")
  print(ds_res[[cl]]$tab)
}
```

## Root

Every node is scored on the germ cell marker sets from the collaborators' S1
sheet: the mean log expression across each set's genes, and the mean percent of
cells detecting each gene. Unless `root_node` is set, the root is chosen by this
lineage's root rule, which names a set and whether the root is the node with its
highest (`max`) or lowest (`min`) mean expression. The scores are written to
`root_marker_set_scores.csv`.

```{r}
germ_sets = c("Primordial germ cells", "Migrating germ cells",
              "Spermatogonial stem cells", "Spermatocytes", "Oocyte")

set_genes = read.csv(paste0(params$project_dir, "/data/", params$marker_file),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(loc_id = trimws(loc_id)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(CellTypeMarkerSet %in% germ_sets) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(set = CellTypeMarkerSet, gene = loc_id)

set_scores = score_marker_sets(combined, merged$node, set_genes) %>%
  dplyr::rename(node = group)

set_table = set_scores %>%
  dplyr::mutate(set          = factor(set, levels = germ_sets),
                node         = factor(node, levels = node_levels),
                mean_logexpr = signif(mean_logexpr, 3),
                pct_detected = round(pct_detected, 1)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(set, node) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(node, n_cells), names_from = set,
                     values_from = c(mean_logexpr, pct_detected),
                     names_glue = "{set}: {.value}") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(node)

write.csv(set_table, file = paste0(results_dir, "/root_marker_set_scores.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

root_rule = switch(lineage,
                   female = params$female_root_rule,
                   male   = params$male_root_rule,
                   all    = params$all_root_rule)
rule_dir  = NA_character_
rule_set  = NA_character_
root_pct  = NA_real_
weak_root = FALSE
n_tied    = 1L

# The root may be given as a node name or as one of the annotations, so it can
# be specified without knowing what number a subcluster came out as.
root_req = as.character(params$root_node)
if (!nzchar(root_req))
  root_req = as.character(switch(lineage,
                                 female = params$female_root_node,
                                 male   = params$male_root_node,
                                 all    = params$all_root_node))

if (nzchar(root_req)) {
  # a node that absorbed another annotated subcluster carries several labels, so
  # the match is against the components rather than the joined string
  has_part = vapply(node_levels,
                    function(nd) root_req %in% node_parts[[nd]], logical(1))

  root = if (root_req %in% node_levels) {
    root_req
  } else if (any(has_part)) {
    hit = node_levels[has_part]
    if (length(hit) > 1)
      stop("the root annotation '", root_req, "' matches more than one node: ",
           paste(hit, collapse = ", "),
           ". That annotation was split across them, so the root has to be named ",
           "by node rather than by label. Set root_node to one of them.")
    hit
  } else {
    stop("root '", root_req, "' is neither a node nor an annotation. Nodes: ",
         paste(node_levels, collapse = ", "), ". Annotations: ",
         paste(sort(unique(unlist(node_parts))), collapse = ", "))
  }
} else {
  rule_parts = regmatches(root_rule, regexec("^(max|min):(.+)$", root_rule))[[1]]
  if (length(rule_parts) != 3)
    stop(lineage, "_root_rule '", root_rule, "' must look like max:<set> or min:<set>")
  rule_dir = rule_parts[2]
  rule_set = trimws(rule_parts[3])
  if (!rule_set %in% germ_sets)
    stop("root rule set '", rule_set, "' is not one of: ",
         paste(germ_sets, collapse = ", "))

  cand = set_scores %>% dplyr::filter(set == rule_set, !is.na(mean_logexpr))
  if (nrow(cand) == 0)
    stop("no genes from the ", rule_set, " set are in the data, so the root ",
         "rule cannot be applied. Set root_node.")

  pick      = if (rule_dir == "max") which.max(cand$mean_logexpr) else which.min(cand$mean_logexpr)
  root      = as.character(cand$node[pick])
  root_pct  = cand$pct_detected[pick]
  weak_root = rule_dir == "max" && root_pct < params$min_detect_pct
  # which.max and which.min take the first of any tie, so report ties
  n_tied    = sum(cand$mean_logexpr == cand$mean_logexpr[pick])
}

if (!root %in% levels(merged$node))
  stop("root '", root, "' is not a node. Nodes: ",
       paste(levels(merged$node), collapse = ", "))

root_type = unique(lineage_key$cell_type[lineage_key$final_label == root])

datatable(set_table, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE, scrollX = TRUE))
```

`r paste0("The ordering is rooted at node **", node_label[root], "**", if (nzchar(root_req)) paste0(", set by the parameter as '", root_req, "'.") else paste0(", the node with the ", if (rule_dir == "max") "highest" else "lowest", " mean expression of the ", rule_set, " set (", lineage, "_root_rule = ", root_rule, ")."), " The root is an assumption. Rooting the same tree elsewhere gives a different ordering.")`

`r if (!is.na(rule_set)) paste0("The ", rule_set, " set chose the root, so its genes rise or fall along pseudotime partly by construction. Do not read their trend as a result.") else ""`

`r if (weak_root) paste0("**The ", rule_set, " genes are barely detected in any node.** The root node detects them in ", round(root_pct, 1), "% of cells on average, below the ", params$min_detect_pct, "% threshold, so the choice rests on noise rather than expression.") else ""`

`r if (n_tied > 1) paste0("**", n_tied, " nodes tie for the ", if (rule_dir == "max") "highest" else "lowest", " ", rule_set, " score.** The root is the first of them in node order, not a distinct choice.") else ""`

```{r, eval=do_markers}
# mean over every pairwise logFC; summary.logFC under pval.type = "some" comes
# from whichever comparison supplied the p-value, so it is not a fixed contrast
marker_effect = function(df) {
  lf = grep("^logFC\\.", colnames(df), value = TRUE)
  if (length(lf) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(df)))
  rowMeans(as.matrix(as.data.frame(df[, lf, drop = FALSE])), na.rm = TRUE)
}

marker_file     = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/subcluster_markers.Rds")
marker_sig_file = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/subcluster_markers_signature.txt")
marker_sig      = paste(obj_sig, paste(node_levels, collapse = ","),
                        paste(as.integer(table(merged$node)), collapse = ","),
                        sep = "|")

if (file.exists(marker_file) && file.exists(marker_sig_file) &&
    identical(readLines(marker_sig_file, warn = FALSE)[1], marker_sig)) {
  sub_markers = readRDS(marker_file)
} else {
  sub_markers = findMarkers(combined, combined$node, test.type = "t",
                            direction = "up", pval.type = "some")
  saveRDS(sub_markers, file = marker_file)
  writeLines(marker_sig, marker_sig_file)
}

sub_marker_tab = purrr::map_dfr(names(sub_markers), function(nd) {
  df = sub_markers[[nd]]
  data.frame(node      = nd,
             Gene      = rownames(df),
             p.value   = df$p.value,
             FDR       = df$FDR,
             meanLogFC = marker_effect(df),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}) %>%
  dplyr::filter(FDR < 0.01, meanLogFC >= params$lfc_thresh) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_description, by = "Gene") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(node) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(meanLogFC), FDR, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(node, Gene, WangGeneID, description, meanLogFC, p.value, FDR)

write.csv(sub_marker_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/subcluster_marker_genes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

marker_counts = data.frame(node = node_levels) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sub_marker_tab %>% dplyr::count(node, name = "n_markers"),
                   by = "node") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(n_markers = ifelse(is.na(n_markers), 0L, n_markers))

datatable(marker_counts, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

## Edge confidence

An MST always returns a tree. It connects every node whether or not the data
supports the connection, so the shape on its own says nothing about how much of
it is real.

Five columns describe each edge from a different direction.

| column | what it is | low | high |
|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | distance between the node centroids | nodes sit close together | nodes are far apart |
| `nn_rank_1`, `nn_rank_2` | each node's place in the other's distance-ordered list | 1 and 1: mutual nearest neighbors | the edge reaches past nearer nodes |
| `separation` | centroid distance in within-node standard deviations | under 1: one continuous population | two distinguishable groups |
| `pct_of_cut` | length as a percentage of the outgroup threshold | the edge survives outgroup splitting | over 100: outgroup splitting removes it |
| `frequency` | percentage of subsampled trees holding the edge | another sample would not have drawn it | drawn whatever the sample |

`frequency` comes from drawing `edge_boot_cells` cells from each node
`edge_boot` times, with replacement, recomputing the centroids and rebuilding
the tree. The count is fixed per node rather than proportional. A node of 5,000
cells has a centroid so precisely estimated that dropping a fifth of them moves
it almost not at all, so a proportional subsample returns close to 100 percent
for every edge including the arbitrary ones. Replacement matters for the small
nodes: drawn without it, a node holding fewer cells than `edge_boot_cells` is
taken whole every time and its centroid cannot move. Read it as a stress test
rather than as a p-value.

A low `separation` is expected between consecutive waypoints on a trajectory.
It is the reading to question where the two nodes carry annotations for distinct
cell types. Combined with the ranks it separates cases that look alike on the
figure.

| `separation` | `nn_rank` | reading |
|---|---|---|
| low | 1 and 1 | one continuous population, joined at its closest point |
| low | high | overlapping nodes, joined the long way round |
| high | 1 and 1 | two distinct groups with a genuine link between them |
| high | high | a long edge to a node that sits near nothing |

No column says whether a low `separation` means the annotation is wrong or the
subclustering was cut too fine. That comes from the marker sets.

```{r}
edge_key = function(a, b) paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b), sep = " -- ")

edge_tab = igraph::as_data_frame(pseudo$mst, what = "edges") %>%
  dplyr::rename(node_1 = from, node_2 = to) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(length = signif(weight, 3),
                key = edge_key(node_1, node_2)) %>%
  dplyr::select(node_1, node_2, key, length)

# The outgroup rule, reported whether or not it is switched on. With
# outgroup = TRUE, createClusterMST puts an artificial node 1.5 times the median
# edge length away from every real node. An edge longer than that is beaten by a
# pair of edges through the outgroup, and deleting the outgroup leaves the tree
# in pieces. The median is taken from the tree built without an outgroup, which
# is the reference the package itself uses.
og_cut = if (is.numeric(params$outgroup)) {
  as.numeric(params$outgroup)
} else {
  ref = if (!isTRUE(params$outgroup)) edge_tab$length else {
    m0 = try(TrajectoryUtils::createClusterMST(
               reducedDim(merged, "corrected"),
               clusters    = as.character(merged$node),
               dist.method = as.character(params$dist_method),
               mnn.k       = params$mnn_k, outgroup = FALSE), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m0, "try-error")) NULL else
      igraph::as_data_frame(m0, what = "edges")$weight
  }
  if (length(ref) == 0) NA_real_ else 1.5 * stats::median(ref)
}

# under 100 the edge survives outgroup splitting, over 100 it is cut
edge_tab$pct_of_cut = if (is.na(og_cut)) NA_real_ else
  round(100 * edge_tab$length / og_cut)

# Two reads on each edge that need no threshold, both from the node centroids of
# the corrected space.
#
#   nn_rank_1   where node_2 sits in node_1's list of nodes ordered by distance
#   nn_rank_2   where node_1 sits in node_2's
#   separation  centroid distance in standard deviations of the within-node
#               spread, so 2 means the centroids sit 2 SD apart
#
# Both are Euclidean, which is what dist.method = "simple" uses. Under any other
# dist.method they describe the corrected space rather than the distances the
# tree was built from.
co_all = reducedDim(merged, "corrected")
nd_all = as.character(merged$node)
cnt    = table(nd_all)
cent   = rowsum(co_all, nd_all)[names(cnt), , drop = FALSE] / as.vector(cnt)

# Per-dimension within-node standard deviation, pooled over the dimensions of
# the corrected space. The distance from a cell to its own centroid is not used
# as the denominator: it grows as the square root of the dimension count while
# the centroid distance does not, so the ratio would shrink as dimensions are
# added. Two nodes four standard deviations apart score 0.56 on that version in
# fifty dimensions and 4 on this one.
node_sd = vapply(rownames(cent), function(g) {
  ix = which(nd_all == g)
  if (length(ix) < 2) NA_real_ else
    sqrt(mean(apply(co_all[ix, , drop = FALSE], 2, var)))
}, numeric(1))

node_dist = as.matrix(dist(cent))
diag(node_dist) = Inf
node_rank = t(apply(node_dist, 1, rank, ties.method = "min"))

edge_tab$nn_rank_1 = node_rank[cbind(edge_tab$node_1, edge_tab$node_2)]
edge_tab$nn_rank_2 = node_rank[cbind(edge_tab$node_2, edge_tab$node_1)]
edge_tab$separation = round(
  node_dist[cbind(edge_tab$node_1, edge_tab$node_2)] /
  ((node_sd[edge_tab$node_1] + node_sd[edge_tab$node_2]) / 2), 2)

n_boot = as.integer(params$edge_boot)
boot_ok = n_boot > 0

if (boot_ok) {
  co   = reducedDim(merged, "corrected")
  nd   = as.character(merged$node)
  by_node = split(seq_along(nd), nd)

  tally = table(unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_boot), function(i) {
    set.seed(1000 + i)
    # stratified, so no node can vanish and change the node set
    # with replacement: a draw without it takes a node of 100 or fewer cells
    # whole every time, so its centroid never moves and its edges read 100 by
    # construction. Drawing with replacement gives every node the same centroid
    # precision whatever its size.
    keep = unlist(lapply(by_node, function(ix)
      sample(ix, max(2L, as.integer(params$edge_boot_cells)), replace = TRUE)))
    m = try(TrajectoryUtils::createClusterMST(
              co[keep, , drop = FALSE], clusters = nd[keep],
              dist.method = as.character(params$dist_method),
              mnn.k = params$mnn_k, outgroup = params$outgroup),
            silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) return(NULL)
    e = igraph::as_data_frame(m, what = "edges")
    unique(edge_key(e$from, e$to))
  })))

  n_done = n_boot
  edge_tab$frequency = round(100 * as.integer(tally[edge_tab$key]) / n_done)
  edge_tab$frequency[is.na(edge_tab$frequency)] = 0

  # edges the resampling drew that the full-data tree did not
  extra = setdiff(names(tally), edge_tab$key)
  extra_tab = if (length(extra) == 0) NULL else
    data.frame(edge = extra,
               frequency = round(100 * as.integer(tally[extra]) / n_done),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      dplyr::filter(frequency >= 10) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(frequency))
} else {
  edge_tab$frequency = NA_integer_
  extra_tab = NULL
}

edge_tab = edge_tab %>%
  dplyr::select(node_1, node_2, length, nn_rank_1, nn_rank_2, separation,
                pct_of_cut, frequency) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(is.na(frequency)), frequency, length)

write.csv(edge_tab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/mst_edges.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# eight narrow columns: no paging unless the tree is large, numbers right
# aligned, and horizontal scroll rather than wrapped headers
datatable(edge_tab, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover",
          options = list(dom = if (nrow(edge_tab) > 25) "tp" else "t",
                         paging = nrow(edge_tab) > 25, pageLength = 25,
                         scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = FALSE,
                         columnDefs = list(list(className = "dt-right",
                                                targets = 2:7))))
```

`r if (!boot_ok || nrow(edge_tab) == 0) "The subsampling check is off. Set edge_boot to a positive number to run it." else paste0("The least confident edge is ", edge_tab$node_1[1], " to ", edge_tab$node_2[1], ", drawn in ", edge_tab$frequency[1], " percent of ", n_boot, " trees built from ", params$edge_boot_cells, " cells per node. ", sum(edge_tab$frequency < 50), " of ", nrow(edge_tab), " edges appear in under half of them, and ", sum(edge_tab$frequency == 100), " in all of them.")`

`r if (is.na(og_cut)) "" else { over = edge_tab %>% dplyr::filter(pct_of_cut > 100); paste0("The outgroup threshold for this tree is ", signif(og_cut, 3), ", which is 1.5 times the median edge length. ", if (nrow(over) == 0) "No edge is longer than that, so outgroup = TRUE returns this same single tree." else paste0(nrow(over), " of ", nrow(edge_tab), " edges are longer: ", paste0(over$node_1, " to ", over$node_2, " at ", over$pct_of_cut, " percent", collapse = ", "), ". Under outgroup = TRUE the tree is rebuilt with the artificial node present, so the pieces are not guaranteed to be this tree minus those edges.")) }`

`r if (!"separation" %in% names(edge_tab)) "" else { far = edge_tab %>% dplyr::filter(pmax(nn_rank_1, nn_rank_2) > 2); ov = edge_tab %>% dplyr::filter(separation < 1); paste0(sum(edge_tab$nn_rank_1 == 1 & edge_tab$nn_rank_2 == 1), " of ", nrow(edge_tab), " edges join mutual nearest neighbors. ", if (nrow(far) == 0) "No edge reaches past a node's two nearest neighbors." else paste0(nrow(far), " reach further than either node's second nearest: ", paste0(far$node_1, " to ", far$node_2, " at ranks ", far$nn_rank_1, " and ", far$nn_rank_2, collapse = ", "), "."), " ", if (nrow(ov) == 0) "Every pair sits at least one standard deviation apart." else paste0(nrow(ov), " pair(s) sit under one standard deviation apart: ", paste0(ov$node_1, " to ", ov$node_2, " at ", ov$separation, collapse = ", "), ".")) }`

## Node graph

Pie charts give the library composition of each node, and the lower panel colors
nodes by mean pseudotime.

Edge color is the percentage of subsampled trees containing that edge. Red edges
are ones a different sample of the same cells would not have drawn, so the
connections they make should not be read as structure. The values are in
`mst_edges.csv`, and `graph_edge_labels` prints them onto the figure. Edges are
drawn plain grey when the subsampling is switched off.

Edge length on this figure is meaningful. The layout is weighted by the real
distance between nodes, so a long edge means the two nodes are far apart in the
corrected space. Those distances are the `length` column of `mst_edges.csv`. The
reproduction is not exact, because a tree in fifty dimensions cannot always be
drawn faithfully in two, but it is close to a uniform rescale rather than
arbitrary. If the message about a failed layout appears above, the figure fell
back to an unweighted layout and edge lengths mean nothing.

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
sample_tally = pt_df %>%
  mutate(node = as.factor(node), library = as.factor(library)) %>%
  group_by(node, library, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  tally()

node_meta = sample_tally %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = library, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  ungroup()
for (l in names(lib_cols)) if (!l %in% names(node_meta)) node_meta[[l]] = 0
node_meta = node_meta %>%
  mutate(totalCells = rowSums(across(all_of(names(lib_cols))))) %>%
  dplyr::rename(name = "node") %>%
  mutate(name = as.character(name))

mean_pseudo = pt_df %>%
  group_by(node) %>%
  summarise(mean_pseudo = mean(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::rename(name = "node") %>%
  mutate(name = as.character(name))

# Edge confidence onto the graph. igraph reports edges in a fixed order and
# as_tbl_graph preserves it, so the column is assigned positionally from the
# same edge list rather than matched back by name.
e_ig = igraph::as_data_frame(pseudo$mst, what = "edges") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(key = edge_key(from, to)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(edge_tab %>%
                     dplyr::mutate(key = edge_key(node_1, node_2)) %>%
                     dplyr::select(key, frequency), by = "key")

# frequency where the subsampling ran, because "drawn in 38 percent of
# subsampled trees" reads without the legend. Gain stays in the table either way.
use_freq  = boot_ok && !anyNA(e_ig$frequency)
e_ig$conf = if (use_freq) as.numeric(e_ig$frequency) else NA_real_
conf_fmt  = function(v) sprintf("%d%%", round(v))

gr = as_tbl_graph(pseudo$mst) %>%
  activate(nodes) %>%
  left_join(node_meta, by = "name") %>%
  left_join(mean_pseudo, by = "name") %>%
  activate(edges) %>%
  mutate(conf = e_ig$conf)

# Layout by real distance. The stress layout ignores edge weights by default and
# draws every edge at roughly the same length, so the picture says nothing about
# how far apart nodes are. graphlayouts treats weights as similarities, not
# distances, so the reciprocal is what is passed: a long edge then has a weak
# pull and is drawn long. On test trees this reproduces the true edge lengths to
# a near-uniform scale factor, correlation 0.999. It also survives a tree split
# into components, which a distance-matrix layout does not.
layout_by_distance = function(graph, lengths) {
  w = as.numeric(lengths)
  w[!is.finite(w) | w <= 0] = min(w[is.finite(w) & w > 0], na.rm = TRUE) / 1000
  out = try(create_layout(graph, layout = "stress", weights = 1 / w), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(out, "try-error")) {
    message("distance-weighted layout failed; falling back to plain stress, ",
            "so edge lengths on the figure will not be meaningful")
    out = create_layout(graph, layout = "stress")
  }
  out
}

set.seed(1)
layout_data = layout_by_distance(gr, e_ig$weight)

# edge midpoints for the numeric labels, from the layout rather than through a
# ggraph label aesthetic, whose arguments vary between versions
e_ig$x = (layout_data$x[match(e_ig$from, layout_data$name)] +
          layout_data$x[match(e_ig$to,   layout_data$name)]) / 2
e_ig$y = (layout_data$y[match(e_ig$from, layout_data$name)] +
          layout_data$y[match(e_ig$to,   layout_data$name)]) / 2
stopifnot(!anyNA(e_ig$x))


# A distance-faithful layout packs tightly related nodes close together, so the
# glyphs have to be sized to the layout rather than fixed. Radius comes from the
# closest pair, with a floor so a very tight pair does not shrink everything to
# nothing. Overlap that remains is informative: those nodes really are that close.
lay_d = as.matrix(dist(as.matrix(layout_data[, c("x", "y")])))
diag(lay_d) = Inf
lay_span = max(diff(range(layout_data$x)), diff(range(layout_data$y)))
layout_data$r = max(min(lay_d) * 0.42, lay_span * 0.012)
pt_size = max(2, min(9, 55 * min(lay_d) / lay_span))

# Confidence is carried by edge color alone. Encoding it as width and color and
# a printed number as well cost two more things to read for no more information.
# The values are in mst_edges.csv and graph_edge_labels puts them back on.
edge_aes = list(
  if (use_freq) geom_edge_link(aes(edge_colour = conf), edge_width = 1.1)
    else geom_edge_link(edge_colour = "grey55", edge_width = 1.1),
  if (use_freq) scale_edge_colour_gradient(low = "#d6604d", high = "#2166ac",
                  name = "% of subsampled trees", limits = c(0, 100)) else NULL)

node_lab = geom_text_repel(data = layout_data, aes(x, y, label = name),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.6, colour = "grey20",
                           min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = .2,
                           segment.colour = "grey60", box.padding = .45,
                           max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1)

edge_lab = if (isTRUE(params$graph_edge_labels))
  geom_label(data = e_ig, aes(x, y, label = conf_fmt(conf)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             size = 2.0, colour = "grey15", fill = "white",
             label.padding = unit(.1, "lines"), label.size = NA) else NULL

gr_pie =
  ggraph(layout_data) +
  edge_aes +
  geom_scatterpie(aes(x, y, r = r), cols = names(lib_cols), data = layout_data,
                  colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Library", values = lib_cols) +
  node_lab + edge_lab +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_void(base_size = 9)

gr_pseudo =
  ggraph(layout_data) +
  edge_aes +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = mean_pseudo), size = max(6, pt_size * 1.6)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "mean pseudotime") +
  node_lab + edge_lab +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_void(base_size = 9)

p_node_graph = (gr_pie / gr_pseudo) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.key.size = unit(.4, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.tag     = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))

p_node_graph

# saved explicitly rather than relying on the last plot, and in both formats:
# pdf for figure assembly, png for slides and email
ggsave(p_node_graph, file = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_node_graph.pdf"),
       width = 7, height = 7)
ggsave(p_node_graph, file = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_node_graph.png"),
       width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

## Marker sets on the tree

The same tree, once per germ cell marker set. Color is the set's mean log
expression scaled to its own maximum, so the panels show where each program sits
rather than how the programs compare with one another. Size is the percentage of
cells in the node detecting the set.

Each panel title carries the set's absolute maximum. A panel whose maximum is
near zero is showing noise stretched across the full color range, so read the
title before the colors. The unscaled values are in `root_marker_set_scores.csv`.

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
graph_sets = trimws(strsplit(as.character(params$graph_marker_sets), ",")[[1]])
graph_sets = intersect(graph_sets[nzchar(graph_sets)], unique(set_scores$set))

set_panel = function(s) {
  sc = set_scores %>% dplyr::filter(set == s)
  mx = suppressWarnings(max(sc$mean_logexpr, na.rm = TRUE))
  ld = layout_data
  ld$rel = if (is.finite(mx) && mx > 0)
    sc$mean_logexpr[match(ld$name, as.character(sc$node))] / mx else NA_real_
  ld$pct = sc$pct_detected[match(ld$name, as.character(sc$node))]

  ggraph(ld) +
    edge_aes +
    geom_node_point(aes(colour = rel, size = pct)) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "expression, relative\nto the set maximum",
                           limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "% of cells detecting",
                          range = c(1.5, 7), limits = c(0, 100)) +
    geom_text_repel(data = ld, aes(x, y, label = name), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                    size = 2.2, colour = "grey25", min.segment.length = 0,
                    segment.size = .2, segment.colour = "grey70",
                    box.padding = .35, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_void(base_size = 8) +
    ggtitle(sprintf("%s  (max %.2f)", s, mx)) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = .5))
}

if (length(graph_sets) > 0) {
  p_set_graph = patchwork::wrap_plots(lapply(graph_sets, set_panel),
                                      ncol = min(2, length(graph_sets))) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
          legend.key.size = unit(.35, "cm"),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 6))

  print(p_set_graph)
  ggsave(p_set_graph, file = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_node_graph_marker_sets.png"),
         width = 11, height = 9, dpi = 300)
  ggsave(p_set_graph, file = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_node_graph_marker_sets.pdf"),
         width = 11, height = 9)
}
```

`r if (length(graph_sets) == 0) "No marker set named in graph_marker_sets is present in the scores." else ""`

## What the ordering tracks

```{r}
lib_r2 = if (dplyr::n_distinct(pt_df$library) > 1)
  summary(lm(pseudotime ~ library, data = pt_df))$r.squared else NA_real_
stage_r2 = if (dplyr::n_distinct(pt_df$stage) > 1)
  summary(lm(pseudotime ~ stage, data = pt_df))$r.squared else NA_real_
```

`r if (is.na(lib_r2)) "All cells come from one library, so library cannot explain pseudotime." else paste0("Library explains ", round(100 * lib_r2, 1), "% of the variance in pseudotime", if (!is.na(stage_r2)) paste0(", and stage explains ", round(100 * stage_r2, 1), "%") else "", ".")`

# Pseudotime-associated genes

Genes changing along each path, tested on uncorrected log counts. All genes at
FDR < `r params$fdr_cut` are written to `tscan_pseudotime_genes.csv`.

```{r}
test_file     = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/tscan_test_pseudotime.Rds")
test_sig_file = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/tscan_test_pseudotime_signature.txt")

pseudo_mat = pathStat(pseudo$ordering)

if (file.exists(test_file) && file.exists(test_sig_file) &&
    identical(readLines(test_sig_file, warn = FALSE)[1], pseudo_sig)) {
  test_pseudo = readRDS(test_file)
} else {
  test_pseudo = TSCAN::testPseudotime(combined, pseudotime = pseudo_mat)
  saveRDS(test_pseudo, file = test_file)
  writeLines(pseudo_sig, test_sig_file)
}

path_genes = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(test_pseudo), function(i) {
  as.data.frame(test_pseudo[[i]]) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Path = names(test_pseudo)[i])
})) %>%
  dplyr::filter(FDR < params$fdr_cut) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_description, by = "Gene") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Direction = ifelse(logFC > 0, "up", "down")) %>%
  dplyr::select(Path, Direction, Gene, WangGeneID, description, logFC, p.value, FDR) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Path, FDR)

write.csv(path_genes, file = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_pseudotime_genes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(path_genes %>% mutate(across(c(logFC, p.value, FDR), ~signif(., 3))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

`r paste0(format(nrow(path_genes), big.mark = ","), " gene-path results at FDR < ", params$fdr_cut, ".")`

## Heatmaps

The 25 most significant genes in each direction along each path.

```{r}
top_by_path = path_genes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(set = paste0(Path, ".", Direction)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(set) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(FDR, desc(abs(logFC)), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 25) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Gene = list(Gene), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# the heatmap's pseudotime bar uses a fixed 0 to 1 color scale
pt_range = range(combined$pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE)
combined$pseudotime_scaled = (combined$pseudotime - pt_range[1]) / diff(pt_range)

heatmaps = list()
for (s in names(top_by_path)) {
  gene_ids    = top_by_path[[s]]
  gene_labels = gene_description$WangGeneID[match(gene_ids, gene_description$Gene)]
  gene_labels = ifelse(is.na(gene_labels), gene_ids, gene_labels)

  path_name   = sub("\\.(up|down)$", "", s)
  cell_subset = rownames(pseudo_mat)[!is.na(pseudo_mat[, path_name])]

  heatmaps[[s]] = plot_pseudotime_heatmap(combined, gene_ids, gene_labels,
                                          cell_subset,
                                          pseudotime_column = "pseudotime_scaled")
}
```

```{r, results="asis"}
for (s in names(heatmaps)) {
  # The heading starts with a word. Pandoc builds anchor ids by dropping
  # everything before the first letter, so a heading of "15.up" becomes the id
  # "up", every path collides, and the table of contents shows a column of
  # "up" and "down" with no path named.
  cat("\n\n### Path ", sub("[.](up|down)$", "", s), ", ",
      sub("^.*[.]", "", s), "\n\n", sep = "")

  # guides = "collect" is what plot_pseudotime_heatmap sets. Rebuilding the
  # patchwork here to change the heights drops it, which leaves the pseudotime
  # legend to render inside a strip 3 percent of the figure height.
  hp = (heatmaps[[s]][[1]] / heatmaps[[s]][[2]]) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(0.03, 1), guides = "collect")
  f  = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_heatmap_",
              gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", s), ".png")
  ggsave(hp, file = f, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

  # The file is written first and then referenced as markdown, rather than
  # printed to the knitr device. In an asis chunk knitr interleaves device
  # output with cat output, and a figure can land under the wrong heading or be
  # dropped. A markdown link is part of the text stream, so the pairing is
  # fixed. Pandoc embeds the file, so the html stays self-contained.
  cat("![](", f, ")\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## GO enrichment of pseudotime-associated genes

GO enrichment for each path and direction, against every gene in the data. Terms
with p < `r params$go_pval` are shown and written to
`tscan_pseudotime_GO_pvalues.csv`.

`r if (!have_go) "Skipped: the GO files were not found." else if (nrow(path_genes) == 0) "Skipped: there are no pseudotime-associated genes to test." else ""`

```{r, eval=have_go && nrow(path_genes) > 0}
path_go = run_go_enrichment(
  gaf              = gaf,
  gene_description = gene_description,
  go_names         = go_names,
  test_genes       = path_genes %>%
                       dplyr::transmute(Gene, set = paste0(Path, ".", Direction)) %>%
                       dplyr::distinct(),
  background_n     = nrow(combined),
  group2_label     = "Path",
  ngroup2_label    = "nPathGenes",
  overlaps_file    = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_pseudotime_GO_overlaps.csv"),
  pvals_file       = paste0(results_dir, "/tscan_pseudotime_GO_pvalues.csv"),
  pval_filter      = params$go_pval)

datatable(path_go %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```
